message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick overview of some key Texas traffic laws and regulations: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55‑mph on rural interstates, 45‑mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways allow drivers to set their own speed as long as it’s safe. | | **Seat Belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited unless you’re using a hands‑free system. | | **DUI Laws** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for most drivers.
• Lower limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at stop signs and yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, give right‑of‑way to vehicles approaching from the right. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children, regardless of direction. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal and check mirrors/blind spots before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is only allowed on multi‑lane roads when the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights, failing to stop at stop signs, and illegal turns are all violations that can lead to fines and points on your license. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, in handicapped spaces without proper permits, or in designated no‑stop zones. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Must have working headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, and a valid registration sticker.
• Mirrors must be properly adjusted and not obstructed. | If you’d like more detailed information on a specific area—like DUI penalties, speeding fines, or school bus rules—just let me know!
